datasets.name: causaldata_gapminder
datasets.licence: CC0-1.0 (gapminder R package)
datasets.note: Life expectancy, population and GDP per capita for 142 countries, every five years 1952-2007. Gapminder via the gapminder R package; used in The Effect, fixed-effects chapter.

datasets.name: causaldata_organ_donations
datasets.licence: MIT (causaldata package); data per original source
datasets.note: Quarterly organ-donation rate for 27 states around California's 2011 policy change (California is the treated group). Kessler & Roth (2014), NBER w20378; difference-in-differences.

datasets.name: causaldata_snow
datasets.licence: MIT (causaldata package); data per original source
datasets.note: John Snow's cholera death rates by water supplier, 1849 and 1854; the `treatment` column is the supplier's water status. Snow (1855), Coleman (2019); difference-in-differences.

datasets.name: causaldata_texas
datasets.licence: MIT (causaldata package); data per original source
datasets.note: State-year panel 1985-2000: prison populations by race and state covariates. Cunningham & Kang (2019); the Mixtape's synthetic-control example, where Texas is treated.

datasets.name: central_bank_rates
datasets.licence: BIS - free use with attribution
datasets.note: Official policy rate, monthly. One row per country per month.

datasets.name: cftc_positioning
datasets.licence: US federal work, public domain. Attribute the CFTC.
datasets.note: Weekly speculative positioning, 1986 onwards. Net non-commercial longs minus shorts as a share of open interest, plus open interest itself. Positioning is as of TUESDAY but published Friday - shift the date forward three days before joining it to prices, or you are trading on information nobody had yet. One contract per commodity (the most-reported one), named in the `contract` column.
datasets.json_note: JSON is thinned to month-end per series for the browser. Use the CSV for anything real - it is complete.

datasets.name: commodities_annual
datasets.licence: World Bank Open Data, CC BY 4.0
datasets.note: Annual nominal USD prices. Units vary by commodity - see the unit column.

datasets.name: companies_top
datasets.licence: Wikipedia CC BY-SA 4.0
datasets.note: Top 10 per year (Forbes Global 2000) plus current top 50 by revenue. list_depth says how deep each list goes - free sources do NOT provide top 100 per year. See the module docstring for how to get that.

datasets.name: crypto_daily
datasets.licence: Bitstamp public market data, free to use. Attribute Bitstamp.
datasets.note: Daily close and volume for five pairs, 2012 onwards. Included as a CONTROL: crypto shares risk appetite with other assets but not the policy rate, the banking system or a lender of last resort, so an event that moves both suggests a sentiment or liquidity channel rather than a policy one. One exchange's tape, not a composite - early years are thin.

datasets.name: elections
datasets.licence: Free for research with attribution. ParlGov (Doring & Manow).
datasets.note: National elections in ~37 democracies since 1900, with turnout where the electorate is known. `severity` is major for early elections - a government falling - and standard for scheduled ones, because that is the distinction that matters when overlaying them on a price.

datasets.name: euro_area_drivers
datasets.licence: Free use with attribution to the European Central Bank.
datasets.note: Euro area policy rates, AAA yield curve, HICP, M3, unemployment and daily EUR reference FX for 31 currencies. The `channel` column matches market_drivers so the two concatenate. FX is EUR-based and quoted once daily - reference rates, not tradeable quotes. RUB ends in March 2022 when the ECB suspended publication.
datasets.json_note: JSON is thinned to month-end per series for the browser. Use the CSV for anything real - it is complete.

datasets.name: fed_communications
datasets.licence: US federal work, public domain. Attribute the Federal Reserve Board.
datasets.note: Every Federal Reserve Board press release the Fed publishes as JSON, typed by the Fed itself. Goes back to 2016 only - that is the extent of the feed, not a filter applied here. Monetary Policy releases are marked major; supervisory and administrative notices are standard.

datasets.note: Monthly geopolitical risk index from newspaper text, 1900 onwards. Threats (GPRT) and acts (GPRA) are separate on purpose - markets tend to move on the threat. 44 country indices included.

datasets.name: geopolitical_risk_daily
datasets.licence: Free for research with attribution. Caldara & Iacoviello (2022), Measuring Geopolitical Risk, AER
datasets.note: Daily geopolitical risk, 1985 onwards, with threat/act split and moving averages.
datasets.json_note: JSON is thinned to month-end per series for the browser. Use the CSV for anything real - it is complete.

datasets.name: georisk_events

datasets.note: Dates the GPR authors annotated as notable geopolitical spikes, with the index level on the day. Researcher-curated, so a higher standard than the Wikipedia-derived rows in political_events.

datasets.licence: Mostly US federal works (public domain); ICE BofA spread indices carry ICE terms. Attribute FRED.
datasets.note: Macro and market series grouped by transmission channel: fx, rates, credit, liquidity, inflation, activity, housing, trade, equity, commodity, uncertainty. Use the channel column to filter. Series that stopped publishing are dropped, not carried forward flat.
datasets.json_note: JSON is thinned to month-end per series for the browser. Use the CSV for anything real - it is complete.

datasets.name: supply_chain_pressure
datasets.licence: Free use with attribution to the Federal Reserve Bank of New York.
datasets.note: Monthly, 1997 onwards. Transport costs plus PMI delivery-time and backlog subcomponents across six economies, expressed as standard deviations from average. Zero is normal. The 2021 peak above 4 is the container crisis. Revised when its inputs revise.

datasets.name: trade_policy_uncertainty
datasets.licence: Free for research with attribution. Baker, Bloom & Davis (2016) QJE; Caldara et al. (2020) JME; Ahir, Bloom & Furceri (2022) NBER WP
datasets.note: Trade policy uncertainty, monthly back to 1960 and daily. Kept apart from general EPU because trade shocks reach FX and commodities through different plumbing than domestic policy fights. TPU_RAW is the article count, TPU the scaled index.

Includes the global index, the European workbook (which is where Germany, France and Italy live - they have no standalone file), 18 country files, and the US categorical breakdown (monetary, fiscal, trade, regulation and so on), which is the part that says WHAT the uncertainty is about.

datasets.name: uncertainty_world
datasets.licence: Free for research with attribution. Baker, Bloom & Davis (2016) QJE; Caldara et al. (2020) JME; Ahir, Bloom & Furceri (2022) NBER WP
datasets.note: IMF World Uncertainty Index, quarterly.
